title: Spinning Loading Border for Loadable Ui Elements
description: Add a uniform loading indicator across the UI: every loadable element (tree items/sections, action buttons, windows, skeleton placeholders) should show a border that spins clockwise with a pulsing motion, in the element's normal border color — gray when unselected, active color when selected/active. Implement in the React component library (ui/js/react/index.tsx + ui/styling/js/ui.css), remove the now-redundant chevron-slot Spinner on tree rows, and mirror the same loading concept + animated border into the wgpu UI (ui/wgpu/rs/lib.rs + framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs) by adding a `loading` field to the shared UiNode schema and rendering an animated rounded-border ring via a new WGSL shader path driven by elapsed time.
summary:
Added a uniform "loading" indicator across the UI: a clockwise-spinning, pulsing border ring in the element's normal border color (gray when unselected/inactive, active color when selected/active).

React (ui/js/react): added `loadingBorderClass`/`loadingBorderActiveClass`/`loadingBorderElementClass`/`loadingBorderStateClass` helpers backed by new `@utility border-loading[-active|-element]` CSS (conic-gradient ring animated via `@property --loading-border-angle`, respects `prefers-reduced-motion`) in ui/styling/js/ui.css. Wired into TreeItem/TreeSection (replacing the old chevron-slot Spinner), Action (also fixed a latent bug where `loading` leaked onto the DOM), Window, DiagramSkeleton, SceneSkeleton, LoadingRow, and the ui-interpreter Suspense fallback + declarative Button control. Extended TreeDataItem/TreeDataSection with a host-declarable `loading` flag ORed with the tree's existing async-loadingById state.

Schema: added `loading: Option<bool>` to the shared UiNode structs (UiStackNode, UiButtonNode, UiSectionNode, UiTreeItemNode, UiTreeSectionNode, UiTreeNode) in ui/wgpu/rs/lib.rs, mirrored in framework/core/js/index.ts, and threaded through the React ui-interpreter mapper so plugin-declared loading state renders identically in both UIs. Golden JSON test stays byte-identical (skip-if-none).

wgpu renderer: added a new `KIND_LOADING_BORDER` draw-instance kind with a WGSL fragment shader branch (clockwise angular sweep + pulse, phase-locked to elapsed time from a new `UiGlobals._pad.x` uniform threaded through `update_globals`/`render_scene_content`/`render_frame`/`render` and populated from `engine_now_ms()` in the framework renderer's per-frame loop). Added `DrawList::push_loading_border` and wired it into `paint_tree_item` (tree rows) and `paint_button` (declarative buttons) using `theme.selected`/`theme.border_normal`.

Tests: extended existing test files only (no new test files) — ui/styling/js/index.test.ts (CSS presence), ui/js/react/index.tsx in-source vitest (class-helper + tree-chrome assertions), ui/wgpu/rs/lib.rs (serde round-trip + a paint test asserting a loading button emits a KIND_LOADING_BORDER instance). Full `cargo test -p ui_wgpu --features engine` passes (78/79; the one pre-existing failure, window_engagement_serializes_to_golden_json, is an unrelated onChange/on_change serde-rename drift from concurrent WIP on WindowEngagementControl). `cargo check -p semio-framework-renderer-wgpu` passes. `bunx vitest`/`bun test` all green for the touched JS/TS packages.

Known gap: UiSectionNode/UiTreeSectionNode loading isn't painted in the wgpu renderer (their paint functions only draw a header strip, not a boxed region suited to a ring) — the schema field exists for forward use but is currently unwired there.
